m.d: A wrinkle is a line or crease on old and fragile skin, usually caused by old age or tiredness.
m.e: My grandfather had a lot of wrinkles on his face.

m.d: To wrinkle is to make lines, creases, or folds on a smooth surface.
m.e: When he smiled, his face wrinkled.

m.d: If you wring something from somebody, you get it from them after hard bargaining.
m.e: The union managed to wring a 4% wage increase from the employer.

m.d: If you wring (out) something wet, you squeeze or twist it tightly to force out the liquid in it.
m.e: Please, wring out the cloth before hanging it up.

m.d: If you wring your hands, you rub them together because you're worried about something.
A wreath is a circular arrangement of flowers, leaves, or branches, often used as a decoration or symbol.
m.e: They hung a wreath on the door for Christmas.

m.d: A wreath is a circular arrangement placed on graves to honour the dead.
m.e: A wreath of poppies was laid at the memorial.

m.d: If x is wreathed in or with y, it is covered or surrounded by it in a circular or curved way.
m.e: Mist wreathed the mountains at sunrise.

m.d: If x is wreathed in or with y, it is decorated with a wreath of y.

m.d: A wrongful heir, possessor, etc. is one that has no right to be in that position.
m.e: The wrongful heir claimed the throne, causing a dispute.
